answer: Every identity is assigned a unique 10 GB shard of the network's shared dataset to guard. Each epoch, identities prove custody by answering random Merkle-proof challenges. An attacker spinning up a hundred fake identities must provision one terabyte of real storage plus bandwidth for each one, since one shard cannot be split or copied to cover two identities. Missed proofs forfeit the identity's deposit. An oasis of free identities dries up when every walnut of claimed data must be cracked open on demand; a meadow of clones is worthless if none of them can feed.
